artists.biography:
Deacon Blue are a Scottish pop band formed in Glasgow during 1985. Their name was taken from the title of the Steely Dan song "Deacon Blues".The current line-up of the band consists of vocalists Ricky Ross and Lorraine McIntosh, keyboard player James Prime and drummer Dougie Vipond.

The band released their debut album, Raintown on 1 May 1987 in the United Kingdom. Their second studio album, When The World Knows Your Name (1989) topped the UK Album Charts for two weeks, and included "Real Gone Kid" which became their first UK top ten single. After releasing further albums in 1991 and 1993, they split up in 1994. Five years later, the band held a reunion gig and this led to a new album, Walking Back Home, with the band now working on a part-time basis; they continue to release new albums, their latest being in September 2012.

perplexity.description:
Ooh Las Vegas" is a compilation album by Scottish rock band Deacon Blue, originally released in September 1990 on the CBS label. The album features a collection of B-sides, unreleased tracks, and songs written for William McIlvanney, showcasing the band's eclectic musical style that blends pop, rock, and jazz influences. Tracks such as "Disneyworld," "Ronnie Spector," and "My America" highlight the group's knack for melodic songwriting and atmospheric arrangements, with touches of jazz-pop and adult contemporary sensibilities woven throughout.

Musically, "Ooh Las Vegas" stands apart from Deacon Blue's main studio albums, offering fans a deeper look into the band's creative process and lesser-known material. Its release came after their successful second album, "When The World Knows Your Name," and provided a bridge between their early pop-rock sound and more experimental tendencies. The album reached number 3 on the UK Albums Chart and remained in the chart for eight weeks, reflecting its commercial appeal. Critics noted its eclectic nature and the quality of its songwriting, cementing its status as a notable entry in Deacon Blue's discography.
